boundary: This is the canonical overall inventory for capability status, dependency order, and assignment. It separates durable product capabilities from operator-owned external evidence, human decisions, and optional optimization; release-readiness authorities remain the delegated validators for their evidence gates. Local or fixture proof can complete a code capability, but it cannot promote hosted, release, or production evidence.
status_boundary: Capability status is a reviewed source-control judgment. Validation checks dependency shape, source anchors, release authority, and package commands without executing proofs or treating ignored target artifacts as fresh evidence.

items.title: Event store and replayable projections
items.summary: Append-only Postgres streams, optimistic concurrency, synchronous projections, and deterministic rebuild audits form the durable state boundary.
complete_when: Committed events rebuild every declared projection without drift.

items.title: Deterministic resolution engine and pack parity
items.summary: The closed rules IR and deterministic resolver cover the full source-derived engine inventory; this is local engine parity, not hosted product readiness.
complete_when: Every actionable in-scope engine inventory row is supported and validated, and every remaining unsupported row is explicitly classified out of scope.

items.title: Capability-gated command runtime
items.summary: Typed commands resolve authority at the boundary, append events transactionally, update projections, and return idempotent acknowledgements.
complete_when: Commands preserve capability, concurrency, idempotency, and event-log invariants through the Postgres pipeline.

items.title: Versioned wire and recoverable live delivery
items.summary: Versioned Rust-owned wire types, REST/JSON commands and cold loads, binary-CBOR WebSocket projection delivery, lag resync, and frontend hydration recovery are locally proven.
complete_when: A seeded client can cold-load, decode only versioned binary-CBOR live frames, recover from lag, and retain capability-filtered state.

items.title: Host setup workbench
items.summary: The host setup role URL drives roster, role, policy, start-phase, stale-command rejection, and recovery through the real command path.
complete_when: A seeded host can configure and start a valid game from the setup role URL and recover from a stale mutation.

items.title: Multi-replica release topology
items.summary: The API now uses shared async object media, migration-free startup, an explicit pre-deploy migrator, and a locally proven two-instance media/live recovery boundary.
complete_when: API startup is migration-free, an explicit migrator owns schema changes, shared S3-compatible media preserves the existing content-addressed contract, and a two-replica local or hosted proof exercises cross-replica media and live recovery.
items.boundary: The local proof drives two API instances against one Postgres pool and one shared object repository: instance A uploads and commands, instance B serves the committed variant, observes the live change, and rehydrates on reconnect. The Railway source contract requires a pre-deploy migrator and two API replicas. This closes the code capability, not hosted race evidence, production promotion, or release readiness.

items.title: 1.0 security release baseline
items.summary: The production frontend uses a browser-proven nonce CSP, release secrets have an environment-isolated custody and rotation contract, deployable images have locked provenance, graph-aware Rust/npm advisory and license policy is proof-enforced, and source plus artifact proofs reject sensitive telemetry.
complete_when: A strict production CSP, secret custody/rotation configuration, dependency/container provenance checks, and no-sensitive-telemetry contracts are enforced and locally proven.
items.boundary: This closes the source-controlled and local-browser security release baseline. The SvelteKit accessibility announcer is the sole inline-style exception and is authorized by an exact CSP hash; executable inline content remains nonce-bound. Secret evidence contains policy and version markers only, never values. Third-party penetration testing, compliance certification, hosted telemetry retention, incident response rehearsal, and production promotion remain independent release evidence.

items.title: Community platform bounded owners
items.summary: RFC 0003 replaced the community catch-all with forum, attention, social, trust_safety, content_reference, and game_platform owners over one rebuildable public-publication index. Search, watches, inbox, mutes, moderation, and citations consume publication identity rather than a closed discussion|game kind switch, so a new public source registers one adapter.
complete_when: The community crate is gone, each RFC 0003 owner exists with its own decide/fold surface, and public engagement consumers depend on publication identity rather than post kind.

items.title: Principal, profile, and privacy boundaries
items.summary: RFC 0004 replaced the generic user record with non-interchangeable Principal, CommunityMembership, PrivacySubject, MemberProfile, and GamePersona concepts. PrincipalId is an opaque UUID at every boundary, ActorId distinguishes Principal from PrivacySubject, profiles carry one active owner, one privacy subject, an encrypted current claim, a keyed handle index, and a stream revision, and public reads (profiles, discussion, search, mutes) resolve attribution only through public_profile, so a private or redacted profile cannot supply it. All five cutover steps landed, including the UUID rebaseline of every principal-bearing relation and wire surface.
complete_when: Typed principal, subject, and profile values are the only profile decision inputs; every canonical authority-bearing principal column is a PostgreSQL uuid; active ownership carries a principal and redacted ownership carries none; and profile, privacy, identity, game, and browser lanes prove the boundaries.

items.title: Executable bounded-context architecture
items.summary: RFC 0006 is a twelve-step atomic migration from the persistence-centred application toward explicit bounded contexts over a typed journal and projector platform. Step 1 landed: tools/architecture_fitness.mjs enforces the active hard bans (pure contexts stay inward-only) and the four integration-hub dependency ratchets, and reports the accepted target bans as explicit migration debt (31 target dependency edges at last count). The remaining steps are architecture migration, not product capability, and are sequenced by the RFC itself; they are recorded here so the RFC's status pointer resolves truthfully rather than to implied completion.
complete_when: All accepted target bans are active hard bans with zero target debt, every production dependency edge conforms to the RFC 0006 target DAG, every event row passes its owning typed codec audit, commands authorize from aggregate or operational authority rather than query projections, the concurrent append/rebuild proof shows no lost projection update, privacy provisioning and erasure crash/retry matrices end in valid states with complete receipts, the catalog proof shows schema ownership and least-privilege grants, the public binary carries no operator/proof or raw privacy-key authority, wire generation proves no internal dependency, and the forced full local proof sweep passes from a reset database.
remaining: Steps 2-12 of the RFC 0006 atomic migration sequence: remove live destructive rebuild authority with a concurrent append/rebuild counterexample; install the context-neutral typed journal; make forum the reference vertical slice with its own application, journal, Postgres, query, and projector owners; cut social, attention, and trust-safety separately; replace commands with GameApplication and GameAggregate; land projector generations; rebuild privacy provisioning and erasure; split schemas, owners, roles, and pools; split runtime processes; rebaseline transport v3; and delete migration debt.
Each landed step must promote the ratchet edges it removes to active hard bans in the same commit; target debt only moves toward zero.

items.title: Reviewable 1.0 core and toolchain
items.summary: Rust 1.95.0 and strict workspace Clippy are proof-enforced; API media, auth, community, game-read, command/import, and live WebSocket delivery, authentication attempt/delivery, provider-neutral identity-delivery cancellation/audit persistence, and live publication, media attached-variant reads, command action submission/validation, host-prompt resolution/replay, DayEvent resolution application, operator-proof report/tool ownership, command verification cost boundaries, domain pack model/validation, resolver intake/suppression/redirect/action/trigger/outcome/trace, projection effect/private-channel, and proof-runner configuration/session-artifact ownership are isolated behind typed boundaries. Pack validation exclusively owns policy admission and resolver action/trigger accessors live with their consuming families. Remaining broad resolver stage coordination, other projection, physical command-test family, and proof-runner scenario/orchestration concentrations remain inventoried.
complete_when: The Rust toolchain is pinned, workspace Clippy is warning-clean, and concentrated pack, resolver, API, projection, command-test, and proof orchestration responsibilities are split into coherent modules without weakening proof coverage.
remaining: Next resolver extraction (queued behind forum editing): Extract the night Protect and Kill stage bodies from crates/domain/src/resolver.rs into a private crates/domain/src/resolver/night_action.rs owner. Introduce typed ProtectionStageContext and KillStageContext inputs that carry prepared actions, validated pack/state, deterministic chance RNG, protection/dependency/effect state, event and trace sinks, kill attribution, and carry tokens without a broad resolver-root facade. Keep action resolution in resolver/action.rs, intake ordering in resolver/intake.rs, trigger fixpoint behavior in resolver/trigger.rs, and policy admission exclusively in pack/validation.rs. Extend the resolver source-boundary contract to fix one coordinator call per stage, direct dependency direction, moved stage ownership, and the absence of local lint suppression. Preserve event and trace order, RNG consumption order, target-state gating, wolf-carry behavior, public resolver APIs, and every golden semantic.
Remove the remaining localized lint expectations and allowances as typed contexts and bounded modules supersede them.

items.title: Seeded playable core loop
items.summary: Seeded host and player role URLs exercise posting, voting, actions, phase resolution, stale recovery, and completion in a real local game.
complete_when: The core live spine completes through browser role surfaces with its saved proof contract green.

items.title: Host and cohost moderation controls
items.summary: Host and delegated cohost controls cover deadlines, phases, prompts, publication, lifecycle changes, completion, conflict rejection, and reload recovery.
complete_when: Every shipped critical moderation control has a typed command, projection result, rejection boundary, and seeded role-surface proof.

items.title: Replacement continuity and authority transfer
items.summary: Replacement preserves slot history while transferring role URLs, sessions, actions, votes, and private-channel authority with stale outgoing denial.
complete_when: Incoming authority recovers across reconnect/reload and outgoing credentials cannot retain current slot capabilities.

items.title: Reveal-gated endgame and vote history
items.summary: Completed games reveal roles and resolved vote history only after completion and preserve them through stale recovery, resync, and reload.
complete_when: Normal and stale player surfaces converge on the same reveal-gated endgame summary and durable vote history.

items.title: Game persona and occupancy epochs
items.summary: GamePersonaRegistered plus SlotOccupancyStarted/Ended are the sole event-sourced authorship and authority substrate. Setup, replacement, live authority, replay/export, projection rebuilds, wire, and browser recovery consume opaque game personas and immutable occupancy epochs without a user-to-slot compatibility path.
complete_when: Named game-scoped personas and stable slots are joined by immutable occupancy epochs, and setup, live authority, replacement, replay, export, projection rebuilds, and browser recovery consume that single model without compatibility aliases.

items.title: Typed DayEvent and reward model
items.summary: A database-free platform model owns validated DayEvent identity, lifecycle, schedules, participation, deterministic resolution evidence, narratives, reward bindings, and concrete effect plans without duplicating the rules engine.
complete_when: Invalid DayEvent states fail closed and valid schedules, decisions, narratives, rewards, and terminal transitions are deterministic values.

items.title: Immutable DayProgram library
items.summary: Hosts select product-visible, versioned, BLAKE3-pinned DayPrograms through a checked-in catalog; the API resolves the authoritative document, verifies pack compatibility, and appends the immutable program plus derived events.
complete_when: A browser can attach only a catalog-published compatible DayProgram reference, and replay remains independent of later catalog changes.

items.title: Scheduled and resolved DayEvent runtime
items.summary: Typed commands, leased scheduler claims, deterministic automatic resolution, host decisions, reward effect application, narrative publication, attention rows, and replayable projections execute DayPrograms through the production transaction boundary.
complete_when: Concurrent scheduler and participant operations converge without duplicate boundaries, rewards, narratives, or projection drift.

items.title: Private DayEvent room lifecycle
items.summary: Private DayEvents derive a stable event channel, grant and revoke membership with participation, transfer access through slot-stable replacement, encrypt private history, and retain read-only history after lock or resolution.
complete_when: Member, withdrawn, replaced, revoked, locked, and non-member role surfaces enforce the same private-room authority across REST, live tickets, media, reconnect, and reload.

items.title: Sixty-player mash acceptance
items.summary: The deterministic local acceptance fixture drives 60 occupied slots, five DayEvents, 300 participant rows, concurrent submissions, two scheduler replicas, public/private narratives, bounded host state, and projection rebuild through production paths.
complete_when: The checked 60-player fixture stays within its contention, query-plan, payload, scheduler, and rebuild regression ceilings.

items.title: Reference-backed private media baseline
items.summary: A command-backed private post reference is checked against the current projection and channel authority at serve time; members receive immutable variant bytes and non-members receive none. Canonical ingest and transcoding are closed by the downstream media capabilities.
complete_when: A command-backed private post serves referenced variant bytes to a member and denies a non-member.

items.title: Canonical private media blob store
items.summary: Bounded local PNG/JPEG ingest applies EXIF orientation, serializes decoder-produced RGBA8 into a versioned canonical record, strips container metadata, derives BLAKE3 identity, and persists it through private fd-relative atomic storage with verified restart lookup; it does not normalize ICC profiles or expose upload, serving, or variants.
complete_when: Malformed and oversized inputs are rejected; metadata is stripped before BLAKE3 identity; equivalent images deduplicate; persistence is atomic and root-confined; restart lookup succeeds.

items.title: AVIF/WebP variant generation
items.summary: A pinned media recipe generates verified thumb, tablet, and full-bounded AVIF/WebP from canonical rasters, commits six private immutable members through a manifest installed last, and reproduces exact bytes across concurrency, restart, and explicit regeneration; this is local recipe proof, not a production codec-quality benchmark.
complete_when: The media core produces validated AVIF/WebP variants for every supported size and can regenerate them from canonical storage.

items.title: Authenticated bounded media upload
items.summary: Server startup now requires a pre-provisioned media root, and an active enabled account can submit bounded raw PNG/JPEG bytes to a prepare-before-persist endpoint that commits one canonical raster plus the fixed six-member variant set and returns only typed immutable handle metadata. Missing, non-account, expired, revoked, disabled, unsupported, mismatched, malformed, dimension-limited, body-limited, and variant-output-limited requests retain no canonical or variant bytes; this is local API/filesystem proof, not post serving, browser, hosted durability, or production upload readiness.
complete_when: Authorized uploads return a persistent handle while malformed, oversized, unsupported, and unauthorized requests fail without retained bytes.

items.title: Uploaded media through a private post
items.summary: An enabled-account player uploads bounded PNG/JPEG bytes, submits only the canonical content id plus alt text, reloads manifest-backed AVIF/WebP from a private post, and a second enabled non-member account receives 403 with a zero-byte body for the exact same URL. This is local scratch-Postgres/filesystem proof, not hosted or object-store durability.
complete_when: A seeded member uploads and posts media, receives the correct variant after reload, and a non-member receives no bytes.

items.title: Mafia private room
items.summary: A real private mafia day-chat room is pack-created, capability-filtered, command-backed, live, reloadable, and denied to non-members.
complete_when: Members can post and recover through the private role URL while non-members never receive room data.

items.title: Role private-message lifecycle
items.summary: The engine declares one slot-stable Role PM per occupied slot; generic private-channel projections and capabilities transfer access on replacement, the incoming account receives private live deltas and durable history/media after reload, and the stale outgoing account receives no thread or media data and cannot append.
complete_when: Role PM creation, membership, posting, receipts, reload, replacement transfer, and stale outgoing denial pass through the real stack.

items.title: Neighborhood, mason, dead, and spectator rooms
items.summary: All supported additional room families are locally complete: pack-declared Mason and Neighbor rooms transfer with stable slots, dead chat follows dead-slot lifecycle authority, and explicit slot-disjoint SpectatorOf grants expose a fixed read-only host-authored room. Each family is encrypted, capability-filtered, live/reload proven, media-authorized, and closed at its stale, non-member, or revoked boundary.
complete_when: Every supported private room family is pack/config-created, encrypted at rest, capability-filtered, replacement-safe, and live/reload proven.

items.title: Account login and account-bound invites
items.summary: Local accounts, opaque sessions, account-bound single-use invites, admin lifecycle controls, and the preserved role-surface adapter are locally proven.
complete_when: A real local account can log in, redeem only its invite, reach the intended role URL, and lose access when disabled or revoked.

items.title: Password storage and rotation security
items.summary: Argon2id storage, authenticated password rotation, session revocation, timing equalization, and bounded credential-attempt state are locally proven.
complete_when: Password verification and rotation preserve equalized failure work, revoke old sessions, and recover after bounded throttling.

items.title: Single-use account recovery
items.summary: Recovery credentials support issue, revoke, consume, expiry, replay rejection, password replacement, and session revocation in the local identity proof.
complete_when: Only one valid recovery credential can replace a password and all invalid, expired, revoked, or replayed credentials fail safely.

items.title: Complete session lifecycle
items.summary: Opaque login, atomic rotation, authenticated logout, password/recovery/disablement invalidation, expiry, and reauthentication preserve the local capability-derived role surfaces and are proven through the scratch-Postgres Chromium identity lane.
complete_when: Login, logout, privilege change, password change, recovery, disablement, expiry, and periodic rotation each enforce the declared session transition.

items.title: Account registration
items.summary: The local registration role URL validates an email-style identifier and password, atomically creates a server-generated unprivileged principal plus opaque session, reaches the seeded game URL in its explicit pending-authority state, and shows duplicate/rate-limit recovery without leaking credentials.
complete_when: A bounded registration route creates an unprivileged account and opaque session, preserves the capability-derived role surface, and rejects duplicate or source-quota attempts with browser-visible recovery.

items.title: Coexisting classic and WorkOS sign-in methods
items.summary: The authentication-method model (principal, methods, one backend-owned app session) is DB-proven end to end: the WorkOS assertion is exchanged once for the same opaque fmss_ session classic uses, a classic method attaches to a WorkOS principal with display-once recovery codes and identical capabilities, removing a method revokes only that method's sessions, the last active method cannot be removed, provider JWTs are rejected as general bearers, and every transition writes identity lifecycle audit rows.
complete_when: One platform principal can authenticate through classic and WorkOS methods interchangeably, convert between them without losing capabilities, and manage methods under recent-authentication, last-active-method, and per-method session-revocation invariants.

items.title: Invite and recovery delivery adapters
items.summary: Invite and recovery issuance seals one-time credentials into redacted typed delivery intents before a lease-claimed provider-neutral outbox worker runs; the scratch-Postgres Chromium lane proves both credential kinds through forced first-attempt failure, declared backoff, provider receipt persistence, GlobalAdmin retry, audit visibility, and the unchanged capability-derived role URL.
complete_when: Invite and recovery delivery are provider-abstracted, retryable, auditable, redacted, and locally testable without claiming live provider traffic.

items.title: Public game index
items.summary: The root board reads a durable public projection of active and completed games, pages by a stable keyset cursor, keeps setup and private lifecycle data out of the query, and is proven through the scratch-Postgres Chromium lane.
complete_when: The public board lists capability-safe active and completed games from a real projection with pagination and browser proof.

items.title: Member data lifecycle and export
items.summary: A typed member lifecycle stream exports personal data, revokes sessions and credentials, removes nonessential identifiers, pseudonymizes retained authorship, and rebuilds affected projections deterministically. The account-security route exposes export and erasure controls, and the retention behavior is documented for policy approval.
complete_when: A member can export their associated account data and request a typed lifecycle transition that revokes authority, erases credentials and nonessential identifiers, pseudonymizes retained authorship, and rebuilds every affected projection deterministically under a declared retention policy.

items.title: Non-game discussion areas
items.summary: Public non-game discussions use a typed forum write model (crates/forum), expected-version appends, active-community-membership and public-profile-backed authorship, independent posting/visibility moderation, canonical topic/post URLs, a public area directory, and a seeded Chromium proof. Topic verbs are create, post, lock/unlock, and hide/unhide; post editing, retraction, and topic curation are tracked separately under product.community.forum-editing-curation.
complete_when: Users can browse, create, post in, and moderate capability-scoped non-game discussions through real routes and projections.

items.title: User profiles
items.summary: Profiles use an active-owner/redacted-attribution model, encrypted private claims, revision-checked owner editing, explicit public or private visibility, and a seeded Chromium proof.
complete_when: A user can view and edit an authorization-safe profile, with durable projection state and browser proof.

items.title: Public community search
items.summary: A rebuildable PostgreSQL full-text projection searches visible discussions, public profiles, active/completed games, and public main-thread posts with weighted rank, stable cursor pagination, typed filters, excerpts, canonical destinations, and synchronous visibility removal.
complete_when: Users can search public discussions, public game threads, profiles, and games through visibility-safe ranked results with stable pagination and canonical result links.

items.title: Public-publication moderation operations
items.summary: Authenticated members can report public discussion and game-thread posts into typed moderation-case streams with active-report deduplication and bounded daily submissions. GlobalMod operators have a capability-safe queue, reporter evidence, reasoned hide/dismiss/restore transitions, append-only history, and synchronous public-thread/search visibility updates.
complete_when: Members can report public discussion and game-thread content into a durable deduplicated queue, and GlobalMod operators can review, reason, action, restore, and audit those reports through capability-safe routes.

items.title: Public watches and unread inbox
items.summary: Authenticated members can watch public discussion topics and public game threads through one durable member-target stream (crates/attention) and advance a monotonic per-watch read cursor. Since RFC 0007 the inbox is reason-derived: member_inbox_item rows are fanned out synchronously for watch and mention reasons, author-self updates are excluded, unread clears from either end, and moderation hide/restore suppresses and restores entries without mutating history.
complete_when: Authenticated members can subscribe and unsubscribe to public topics and public game threads, receive a durable privacy-safe in-app update inbox, and advance a per-subscription read cursor without polling private audiences or exposing credential principals.

items.title: Personal community mute controls
items.summary: Authenticated members own durable private mute relationships whose read-time overlays suppress public-profile contributions across discussion, search, public game threads, and watched inboxes without changing anyone else's view.
complete_when: Authenticated members can mute and unmute public profiles through a durable private relationship stream, inspect their bounded mute list, and have muted authors consistently suppressed from personalized discussion, search, and inbox reads without changing global visibility or exposing credential principals.

items.title: First-class quotations and citations
items.summary: RFC 0002: a quotation is a typed, same-thread, write-time-validated fact on the citing post with an immutable excerpt snapshot. Forum and game keep separate decide paths over the shared content_reference validator, the quoted-by reverse index is a rebuildable projection, and composer and renderer surfaces exist on discussion topics and public game threads.
complete_when: Members can attach validated same-thread quotations in discussion and game composers, quoted posts expose a rebuildable quoted-by index, and visibility overlays apply to citations at read time.

items.title: Closed community admission and sponsorship provenance
items.summary: RFC 0005: community membership is an aggregate admitted by exactly one single-use, target-bound invitation issued by an active sponsor; founders are explicit. Sponsorship lineage is an immutable acyclic forest with a rebuildable closure, private to the member and global stewards. Forum posting and topic creation require an active membership binding, sponsor suspension revokes pending invitations without cascading to descendants, and stewards suspend, restore, and revoke through capability-safe admin routes.
complete_when: Unknown identities cannot self-provision, every ordinary membership traces to one accepted invitation, community-member authority resolves from the active-membership projection, and stewards can inspect lineage and sanction memberships through proven routes.

items.title: First-class mentions and addressed delivery
items.summary: RFC 0007: a mention is a validated span on the post, not markup. Community mentions address currently-public profiles and deliver to the reason-derived member inbox; game mentions address a slot that can read the channel and deliver through a sibling slot_mention_notification table, never to a principal. Typeahead lives in the existing composer, mute and moderation overlays stay at read time, and per-post mention bounds are enforced at decision time.
complete_when: Members can mention public profiles in discussions and readable slots in game channels through the composer, mentioned parties receive privacy-safe addressed delivery that clears from either end, and no mention path exposes a credential principal.

items.title: Forum post editing and topic curation
items.summary: The forum write model has nine verbs: create topic, submit post, edit post, retract post, lock/unlock, hide/unhide, rename, move, pin (crates/forum/src/lib.rs). Authors edit their own posts inside forum::FORUM_EDIT_WINDOW_SECONDS with append-only revision history (migration 0012, discussion_post_revision) and retract them as a read-time overlay that preserves cited excerpts; GlobalMod renames, moves, and pins topics through POST /discussions/topics/{topic}/curation (migration 0013), pinned topics lead an area's first page without touching the keyset, a moved topic keeps resolving under its old area URL and the page redirects to the canonical one, and post publication hrefs follow the move. Owner ruling 2026-09-16: editability is a policy owned by each thread source, not a platform-wide capability. Forum threads are editable within a bounded window; game channel threads are never editable because posts are slot-authored evidence in a live game, and the absence of any game edit command is a proven contract (api::public_platform_http_boundary::game_threads_have_no_edit_or_retract_path), not an omission. A future signup or recruitment thread kind declares its own edit policy when it is added.
complete_when: A forum post author can edit their own post within a bounded window with an append-only revision history and a visible edited marker, can retract their own post as a read-time overlay that preserves history and cited excerpts, and a GlobalMod can rename, move, and pin a topic through capability-safe routes; search, inbox, citation, and moderation overlays stay consistent; game channel posts remain provably non-editable; and a seeded Chromium proof covers each flow.

items.title: Signup threads linked to spawned games
items.summary: A signup thread is an ordinary forum topic that a game names as its origin at creation. Design ruling 2026-09-16: the game declares the link as one immutable, additive origin fact on GameCreated (CreateGame { origin: Option<PublicContentRef> }), validated at decide time against a visible public forum topic through projection reads; the forum write model never learns about games (RFC 0003 invariant 1). 'Signup' is a derived kind, not a declared one: a topic is a signup thread iff a game names it, so there is no topic kind column and no dual state. Forward (game -> origin topic) lives on game_index, the reverse index (topic -> spawned games) is a rebuildable projection fed by the game source adapter, and an optional reason-derived inbox reason tells topic watchers when the game spawns. Grouping is a discussion_area with slug signups, which is existing data. Signup threads inherit the forum edit policy from product.community.forum-editing-curation.
complete_when: A host can name a visible public forum topic as a game's origin at creation, the origin is immutable and validated at decide time, the topic page shows its spawned games and the game surfaces link back to the origin topic from rebuildable projections, watchers of the origin topic receive a reason-derived inbox update when the game spawns, and a seeded Chromium proof covers the flow.
remaining: Add the optional origin to wire Command::CreateGame and the GameCreated payload; in commands::create_game validate through projection reads that the origin is a PublicContentRef to a visible forum topic (host-authored unless the owner relaxes that to any member topic), and record the origin as immutable.
Add game_index.origin_topic_id and a rebuildable discussion_topic_spawned_game reverse index fed by the game source adapter in projections::publications, with rebuild-audit coverage.

Extend wire GameIndexEntry with origin_topic and DiscussionTopic with spawned_games; render the origin picker in the host setup workbench, a spawned-game banner on the topic page, and an origin link on game surfaces.
Register an attention adapter for a game_spawned_from_watched_topic inbox reason; do not auto-watch or auto-lock the origin topic.
Extend the game-index and discussion role proofs with an origin-linked game and update docs/arch/01-domain-model.md and 10-event-schema.md.
items.decision_trigger: Introduce a dedicated Signup context with typed Enrol, roster, waitlist, and quota commands only when enrolment must be machine-readable (auto-seating from a roster, waitlists, or quotas). Until then the host reads the thread and seats players with SeatPersona; posts are never parsed as enrolments.

recommended_slice.objective: Add signup threads as an edge from a game to an ordinary forum topic. Extend wire Command::CreateGame with origin: Option<PublicContentRef> and thread it through commands::create_game, which validates via projection reads that the origin names a visible public forum topic (host-authored unless the owner relaxes that) and records it as an additive, immutable origin key on the GameCreated payload; the forum never learns about games and no kind column is introduced. Add migration 0014 with game_index.origin_topic_id and a rebuildable discussion_topic_spawned_game reverse index fed by the game source adapter in projections::publications, with rebuild-audit coverage. Extend wire GameIndexEntry with origin_topic and DiscussionTopic with spawned_games; render an origin picker in the host setup workbench, a spawned-game banner on the topic page, and an origin link on game surfaces. Register an attention adapter for a game_spawned_from_watched_topic inbox reason without auto-watching or auto-locking the origin topic. Extend the game-index and discussion role proofs with an origin-linked game and update docs/arch/01-domain-model.md and 10-event-schema.md.
non_claims: Do not add a kind column to discussion_topic or teach the forum crate about games; the signup kind is derived from the game-to-topic edge.
Do not build enrolment, roster, or machine-readable signup state; the dedicated Signup aggregate waits on the recorded decision trigger.
Do not auto-watch or auto-lock the origin topic, and do not let a game change its origin after creation.
Do not allow more than one origin per game; many games per topic remain allowed.

items.title: Per-member posting rate limits
items.summary: Posting has no rate control. The only rate limits in the runtime govern authentication failures (crates/api/src/authentication.rs), and capacity admission (docs/arch/12-capacity-and-overload.md) bounds concurrency: a global in-flight ceiling plus a one-command-per-principal fence. Neither bounds how often a member may post, so one compromised or hostile account can flood a discussion topic, a game thread, a report queue, or mention delivery at the speed of sequential requests. Closed admission lowers the probability but not the blast radius. The limit belongs at the application boundary as a typed, per-principal, per-surface budget with a retryable rejection; it is not a moderation sanction and records no durable event.
complete_when: Topic creation, discussion posts, game-thread posts, post edits, moderation reports, and mention fan-out each enforce a declared per-principal budget; an over-budget request receives a typed retryable rejection carrying Retry-After that the composer surfaces without losing the draft; hosts and GlobalMods have a documented exemption policy; the budgets are runtime configuration with redacted debug output; and command-level and seeded browser proofs cover acceptance, rejection, window reset, and exemption.
remaining: Owner decision: default budgets per surface (for example posts per minute and topics per hour) and whether game hosts and cohosts are exempt inside their own games.
Add a bounded per-principal rate store, reusing the authentication limiter's window and lockout shape rather than a second mechanism, and a typed rate-limited rejection code on the wire.
Enforce the budget at discussion topic/post/edit, game thread post, moderation report, and mention admission, before any event is appended.
Surface Retry-After in the discussion and game composers while retaining the unsent body, and extend the discussion and core-live role proofs with an over-budget case.
Document the budgets and the rejection in docs/arch/12-capacity-and-overload.md.

items.title: Batched citation previews on topic pages
items.summary: The discussion topic page loader requests quoted-by previews with one API call per cited post (loadCitationPages in frontend/src/routes/discussions/[slug]/t/[topic]/+page.server.js), up to one per post on a 50-post page. Each call runs its own visibility-overlay query through projections::visible_public_incoming_citations. Page cost therefore grows with how often a thread is quoted, which is exactly the shape of a busy mafia discussion. A single page-scoped read returning previews for every cited post removes the fan-out without changing the citation model.
complete_when: A topic page load issues one bounded citation-preview read for the whole page regardless of how many posts are cited; the batched read applies the same visibility, retraction, hide, and mute overlays as the per-post route; a query-plan or row-count regression ceiling guards it; and the discussion role proof still shows quoted-by previews.
remaining: Add a page-scoped projection read returning bounded incoming-citation previews for a set of source sequences in one topic, with the per-post overlays applied in SQL.
Expose it as one API route keyed by topic and a bounded source_seq list, and replace loadCitationPages with a single call.
Keep or remove the per-post citations route according to remaining callers, and add a regression ceiling on queries per page load.

items.title: Safe post formatting, links, and spoilers
items.summary: Post bodies render as plain text with preserved whitespace plus mention links (bodySegments in frontend/src/lib/app/mention-model.mjs; white-space: pre-wrap in the topic page). URLs are not clickable, and there is no emphasis, block quote, list, code, or spoiler markup. Spoilers matter in particular for a mafia community: reviews and completed-game discussion depend on them. The stored body stays the authored text so that quotations, revision history, search, and game evidence are unchanged; formatting is a small, closed, read-time grammar parsed into typed segments and rendered without {@html}, so the strict production CSP (frontend/svelte.config.js) and the existing mention segments survive intact.
complete_when: Discussion and game-thread posts render one shared, closed formatting grammar (at minimum paragraphs, emphasis, links with safe rel and scheme allowlist, block quotes, inline and block code, and collapsible spoilers) through typed segments without raw HTML injection; the composer offers preview; search and quotation excerpts index and cite the plain text; malformed or hostile markup degrades to literal text; property or fuzz tests cover the parser; and seeded browser proofs cover rendering, spoiler reveal by keyboard and pointer, and CSP cleanliness.
remaining: Owner decision: the grammar (a restricted Markdown subset or phpBB-style tags familiar to the community) and whether game hosts may disable formatting per game.

Implement one parser producing typed segments that composes with mention segments, shared by the discussion and player-thread models, with a scheme allowlist for links and literal fallback for anything unrecognized.
Render the segments in the discussion and player thread without {@html}, add an accessible spoiler disclosure, and add composer preview.
Ensure search documents, quotation excerpts, and inbox previews use the plain-text projection of the body.
Add parser property tests and extend the discussion, core-live, and CSP browser proofs.

items.title: Image attachments in public forum posts
items.summary: Uploaded media reaches only game thread posts: wire SubmitPost carries media and commands validate it (MAX_THREAD_POST_MEDIA in crates/commands/src/lib.rs), while forum::TopicCommand::SubmitPost has no media field. The upload, canonical blob store, and AVIF/WebP variant pipeline are complete and content-addressed, but serving is private and membership-gated. Public forum media needs a public-publication serving path whose visibility follows the post: a hidden, retracted, or erased post must stop serving its bytes to readers while retained moderator evidence stays available to GlobalMods.
complete_when: A member can attach a bounded number of uploaded images with required alt text to a discussion post or topic opener; readers receive the correct variant through a public serving route whose authorization follows the post's publication visibility, so hide, retract, and data-lifecycle erasure stop reader delivery while GlobalMod evidence access remains; edits cannot swap media outside the edit rules; and seeded browser proofs cover attach, render, hide, and denied delivery.
remaining: Owner decision: whether attachments may be added or removed by an edit inside the edit window, and the per-post image limit.
Add media references to the forum post events and PostState, validated against the uploader's own upload handles, with an additive migration for the post-media relation.
Add a public-publication media route authorized by the post's current visibility overlays, and a GlobalMod evidence path for hidden content.
Add attach and alt-text controls to the discussion composer and render variants in the topic page.
Extend docs/arch/07-images.md and the discussion role proof.

items.title: Member-to-member private conversations
items.summary: Private messaging exists only inside games (role PMs and pack-created rooms, product.private.role-pm), scoped to slots and occupancy epochs. Members have no way to message each other outside a game, which a community forum needs for hosting, replacements, and ordinary coordination. This is a new bounded owner, not an extension of game rooms: conversations are addressed to profiles, respect member mutes in both directions, feed the inbox, are encrypted at rest like private rooms, are reportable, and participate in export and erasure.
complete_when: A community member can start a private conversation with one or more members, post, and receive inbox deliveries; a muted or suspended party cannot initiate or deliver; participants can leave; content is encrypted at rest, excluded from public search, reportable with a stated moderator-access policy, and included in member export and erasure; and seeded browser proofs cover start, reply, mute denial, report, and export.
remaining: Owner decision: group conversation limit, whether GlobalMods can read a conversation only through a participant's report or also directly, and retention after all participants leave.
Write a short RFC for the conversation owner, placing it in the RFC 0006 target DAG so it is born conforming rather than adding ratchet debt.
Implement the conversation aggregate, encrypted projection, inbox reason, mute and suspension checks, and report target.
Add conversation list and thread routes, export and erasure coverage, and a seeded role proof.

items.title: Opt-in email notifications for the inbox
items.summary: The in-app inbox is durable and reason-derived, but nothing reaches a member who is not looking at the site. The only outbound delivery is identity mail (invites and recovery) through the provider-abstracted, retryable, audited IdentityDeliveryGateway in crates/api/src/identity_delivery.rs. Notification mail should reuse that delivery machinery with its own admission and budget: opt-in per reason, a batched digest rather than per-event mail, a one-click unsubscribe, and no private content — no game-room, PM, or conversation bodies — in the message.
complete_when: A member can opt in per inbox reason to immediate or digest email; deliveries batch unread inbox items, never include private-channel content, carry a signed one-click unsubscribe, respect mutes and suspension, stop on data-lifecycle transitions, reuse the audited provider gateway with its own retry and quota budget, and are covered by a local fake-provider proof without claiming live provider traffic.
remaining: Owner decision: default opt-in state, digest cadence, and whether mention and spawned-game reasons are eligible for immediate mail.
Add per-member notification preferences and a digest scheduler that claims unread inbox items idempotently.
Generalize the delivery gateway admission so notification mail cannot starve invite and recovery delivery.
Add signed unsubscribe, preference UI, and a fake-provider delivery proof; extend the product policy draft with notification retention.

items.title: Portable completed-game export
items.summary: Completed games export a versioned checksum-bearing event manifest through a host role URL; isolated import, projection rebuild, replay audit, and tamper rejection are locally proven.
complete_when: A completed game exports its events, schema/version metadata, referenced projections/media manifest, checksum, and deterministic import/audit result.

items.title: Real hosted identity evidence
items.summary: Local identity code and packet validators are not live hosted account, invite, recovery, abuse-control, session-secret, or retention evidence.
complete_when: A non-fixture redacted operator packet records passed real hosted identity lifecycle and role-surface evidence for every required family.
remaining: Deploy the identity lifecycle and attach real redacted retained/exportable evidence for every hosted family.
blocked_on: Real hosted identity target and operator evidence packet

items.title: Hosted API/frontend deployment evidence
items.summary: Local and hosted-like proof cannot establish an externally reachable deployment or external health checks.
complete_when: Externally reachable API and frontend targets pass the real-hosted preflight and raw-capture contract without fixture or synthetic inputs.
remaining: Provision the hosted target and capture non-synthetic external frontend/API health and flow evidence.
blocked_on: Externally reachable deployment and raw operator capture

items.title: Hosted demo fixtures and sanitized-data policy
items.summary: Local seed fixtures do not prove a hosted demo environment, sanitized data policy, or release-safe invite delivery.
complete_when: The hosted demo target is reproducibly seeded from sanitized policy-approved data and its invite delivery is release-safe.
remaining: Provision and audit hosted demo data, reset policy, and invite delivery.
blocked_on: Hosted demo environment and operator-approved sanitized-data policy

items.title: Production backup and recovery evidence
items.summary: The local backup/restore drill is baseline proof only; it does not establish production storage, PITR, key escrow, or secret rotation.
complete_when: A production-like backup, PITR restore, key escrow, and secret-rotation drill produces retained operator evidence.
remaining: Run and retain the production-like backup/PITR, escrow, and rotation drill.
blocked_on: Production-like storage, keys, secrets, and operator access

items.title: Real hosted concurrent-race evidence
items.summary: The promoted local race matrix does not prove multi-node hosted races, reload/reconnect convergence, or hosted stale-client behavior.
complete_when: The real hosted matrix executes concurrent commands across the deployed topology and records reload, reconnect, and stale-conflict convergence.
remaining: Execute and retain the non-fixture multi-node hosted race matrix.
blocked_on: Stable real hosted topology and external race capture

items.title: Real hosted observability and operations evidence
items.summary: Local structured logs and hosted-like signal bundles do not prove hosted logs, metrics, traces, paging/SLOs, or incident response.
complete_when: The deployed target emits retained logs, metrics, traces, alerts/SLO evidence, and an exercised incident-response receipt.
remaining: Capture real hosted telemetry, alerting/SLO, paging, and incident-response evidence.
blocked_on: Hosted telemetry stack and operator incident-response exercise

items.title: Human beta/release approval
items.summary: No coding agent or generated artifact can approve release ownership, rollback readiness, or support staffing.
complete_when: The release owner reviews product scope and all external evidence, verifies rollback/support staffing, and records explicit approval.
remaining: Obtain and record explicit human release-owner approval after all prerequisites close.
blocked_on: All required product capabilities and operator-owned release evidence

items.title: Record the strict vote-syntax decision
items.summary: Player vote targets are server-supplied controls that emit typed vote commands; the governing docs record that posts are never parsed as votes.
complete_when: The domain and roadmap docs record the shipped strict-target decision and remove the stale open call.

items.title: Ratify the fmarch codename
items.summary: The owner ratified fmarch and the governing architecture, repository, package, domain, and deployment names agree.
complete_when: The owner ratifies the name and the vision/index docs consistently use it.

items.title: Human assistive-technology release review
items.summary: Synthetic interaction checks do not establish that the critical 1.0 journeys work with a real keyboard and screen reader.
complete_when: A retained human keyboard and screen-reader packet covers the critical identity, public, player, host, moderation, inbox, and mute journeys and records successful reruns after every critical fix.
remaining: Run, retain, remediate, and rerun the critical keyboard and screen-reader journey matrix.

items.title: Privacy, terms, retention, and moderation policy approval
items.summary: The codebase does not yet carry owner-approved public policy for data use, retention, acceptable use, moderation, appeals, and support.
complete_when: The operator approves and publishes policy text consistent with the implemented member data lifecycle, retention boundaries, moderation process, appeal route, and support ownership.
remaining: Draft, review, approve, publish, and link the privacy, terms, retention, acceptable-use, moderation-appeal, and support policies.

items.title: Projection snapshots
items.summary: Snapshots are a discardable replay optimization and are excluded from required completion until measured replay cost demands them.
complete_when: A measured replay SLO breach is addressed by versioned discardable snapshots with deterministic fallback to full replay.
remaining: Define a replay benchmark and SLO before deciding whether snapshot implementation is warranted.
items.decision_trigger: Promote only when a representative long-game replay benchmark exceeds the declared latency or resource SLO.

items.title: Public history explorer
items.summary: The accepted public-knowledge-as-of explorer remains a post-1.0 presentation capability; 1.0 requires the persona/occupancy truth model it will consume, not the explorer UI itself.
complete_when: Active and completed public games expose server-authoritative snapshot-plus-timeline replay with stable exact-moment links and the RFC's redaction boundary.
remaining: Implement the public replay query, fold, exact-moment links, and explorer surface after the required 1.0 persona/occupancy substrate and release closure are complete.
items.decision_trigger: Promote only after required 1.0 platform scope is complete and the owner explicitly opens the post-1.0 public-history product frontier.

items.title: Reactions, polls, bookmarks, and drafts
items.summary: Common forum conveniences that a mafia community can do without at 1.0: post reactions, topic polls, personal bookmarks, and server-side draft persistence. Each is a separate small owner or projection. They stay outside required completion so that robustness and the core reading and writing experience land first.
complete_when: Each promoted extra ships as its own capability item with typed commands, rebuildable projections, mute and moderation overlays where content is involved, and a seeded browser proof.
remaining: Split each extra into its own registry item when promoted, with a recorded owner decision on scope.
items.decision_trigger: Promote an individual extra only after required 1.0 platform scope is complete, or earlier when the owner records a community request that the existing features cannot meet.

orchestration_rules: The default coding selector may choose only dependency-satisfied incomplete code items; external evidence and human approval never become coding-agent work.
One integrator owns main, central registries, canonical artifacts, commits, and pushes; reviewers remain read-only while a slice is active.
A product-facing capability closes only with its listed acceptance evidence and explicit proof boundary; additional wrappers or commits are not progress by themselves.
Local, fixture, and hosted-like evidence may prepare operator handoffs but cannot complete an external-evidence item.
Optional work remains outside required completion until its decision trigger fires.
